Nicholas Sofroniew

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: In this paper, we provide evidence that LLMs do possess such workspace-like representations.

span.label: global workspace / conscious-access-like representations in large language models
span.quote: Specifically, we observe that language models maintain a privileged set of internal representations, available for report, modulation, and flexible internal reasoning, atop a much larger volume of automatic processing.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: The Jacobian lens is a technique for inspecting the contents of the residual stream at these intermediate layers.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A CONSTRUCT IS DEFINED BY ANALOGY TO ANOTHER FIELD'S CRITERIA, AND THE ANALOGY IS THE DEFINITION RATHER THAN A MOTIVATION FOR IT: we **DEFINE A SUBSET OF VECTOR REPRESENTATIONS AS WORKSPACE-LIKE IF IT SATISFIES THE FOLLOWING PROPERTIES**, which **MIRROR THE PROPERTIES CHARACTERISTIC OF CONSCIOUS ACCESS** described above. What makes something a member of the new category is that it satisfies conditions imported from a theory about brains
span.quote: define a subset of vector representations as workspace-like if it satisfies the following properties, which mirror the properties characteristic of conscious access described above

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AND THE PAPER'S OWN LIMITATIONS SECTION SAYS THE DISTINCTION IT RELIES ON HAS NO PRINCIPLED DEFINITION: this judgment **WAS SOMEWHAT POST-HOC**, and **WE DID NOT PROVIDE A PRINCIPLED DEFINITION OF WHAT DISTINGUISHES A “WORKSPACE” REPRESENTATION FROM A “MOTOR” ONE**. The boundary was drawn empirically and the criterion for it is declared absent, by the people who drew it, in the same paper that uses it throughout
span.quote: But this judgment was somewhat post-hoc, and we did not provide a principled definition of what distinguishes a "workspace" representation from a "motor" one.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE MISSING CRITERION IS SPECIFIED AS A CHOICE BETWEEN TWO REPAIRS, NEITHER OF WHICH IS PERFORMED: **A FULLER ACCOUNT WOULD EITHER SUPPLY SUCH A PREDICTIVE CRITERION, OR WOULD REPLACE THE FLEXIBLE/AUTOMATIC DISTINCTION WITH SOMETHING MORE PRECISE**. What would fix the vocabulary is stated exactly, and left as a description of a paper someone else could write
span.quote: A fuller account would either supply such a predictive criterion, or would replace the flexible/automatic distinction with something more precise.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AND THE REASON THE CRITERION IS NEEDED IS GIVEN AS AN INABILITY, NOT A DIFFICULTY: the tasks were chosen **BECAUSE THE FLEXIBLE/AUTOMATIC DISTINCTION IS CLEAR FOR THEM**; however, for many tasks of practical interest **IT IS NOT**, and **WE HAVE NO WAY OF PREDICTING IN ADVANCE, FOR AN ARBITRARY COMPUTATION, WHETHER IT WILL ENGAGE THE J-SPACE**. The cases were selected for the property that the distinction applies to them, and that selection is disclosed
span.quote: The tasks in §3.5 were chosen because the flexible/automatic distinction is clear for them; however, for many tasks of practical interest it is not, and we have no way of predicting in advance, for an arbitrary computation, whether it will engage the J-space.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A CONCEPT IS DEFINED AS WHATEVER THE SYSTEM ITSELF LATER PRODUCES, AND THE CIRCULARITY IS THE POINT OF THE EXPERIMENT: **HERE WE DEFINE THE REACTION CONCEPT TO BE WHATEVER ANSWER THE MODEL ITSELF GOES ON TO PRODUCE**, so the question is whether the model's eventual choice **IS ALREADY IN THE LENS WHILE IT READS THE INSTRUCTION TO WITHHOLD IT**. The definition has no content until the system has acted, which is what makes the test possible
span.quote: here we define the reaction concept to be whatever answer the model itself goes on to produce, so the question is whether the model's eventual choice is already in the lens while it reads the instruction to withhold it.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A METHOD IS DEFINED BY THE QUESTION IT ASKS RATHER THAN BY WHAT IT MEASURES, AND CONTRASTED WITH THE METHOD IT REPLACES: the J-lens provides a complementary way of interpreting a feature - **IT ASKS WHAT THE FEATURE DIRECTION IS VERBALIZABLE AS, INDEPENDENT OF WHERE IT FIRES**. The older method is said to **MISLEAD WHEN THE FEATURE ENCODES AN ABSTRACT ASSESSMENT WHOSE SURFACE TEXTUAL CORRELATES ARE INCIDENTAL**
span.quote: The standard approach to interpreting an SAE feature is to inspect the contexts on which it activates most strongly. This works well when the feature's meaning is apparent from its superficial contexts, but can mislead when the feature encodes an abstract assessment whose surface textual correlates are incidental. The J-lens provides a complementary way of interpreting a feature: it asks what the feature direction is verbalizable as, independent of where it fires.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AN ANALOGY IS ASSERTED AND ITS LIMIT IS STATED IN THE SAME SENTENCE, WITH THE UNCLAIMED PART SPELLED OUT: despite these similarities, **WE DO NOT CLAIM THAT LANGUAGE MODELS REPRODUCE THE FULL ARCHITECTURE GLOBAL WORKSPACE THEORY ASCRIBES TO THE BRAIN** - specialized, encapsulated processors competing for entry to a workspace that broadcasts back to them through recurrent connections. The borrowed theory is named in full precisely where the borrowing stops
span.quote: Despite these similarities, we do not claim that language models reproduce the full architecture global workspace theory ascribes to the brain—specialized, encapsulated processors competing for entry to a workspace that broadcasts back to them through recurrent connections

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE DISANALOGY IS PUT FIRST AND THE EXPECTATION DENIED: **IT IS NOT OBVIOUS THAT THEY SHOULD**; in the brain, the workspace is closely associated with recurrent dynamics and brain region interactions **THAT HAVE NO DIRECT ANALOG IN THE TRANSFORMER ARCHITECTURE** on which LLMs are based. The reason the finding would be surprising is given before the finding is defended
span.quote: It is not obvious that they should; in the brain, the workspace is closely associated with recurrent dynamics and brain region interactions that have no direct analog in the transformer architecture on which LLMs are based.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: TWO EXPLANATIONS OF THE PAPER'S CENTRAL FINDING ARE OFFERED AND NEITHER IS CHOSEN: in this view, the workspace **IS VERBALIZABLE BECAUSE THE MODEL'S OUTPUT SPACE IS VERBAL**, and the format in which it broadcasts intermediate results to itself **IS SHAPED BY THE FORMAT IN WHICH IT MUST EVENTUALLY ACT**. The property named in the title is explained by the shape of the output channel rather than by anything about the representation
span.quote: In this view, the workspace is verbalizable because the model's output space is verbal, and the format in which it broadcasts intermediate results to itself is shaped by the format in which it must eventually act.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A SCOPE LIMIT IS STATED WITH A COINED METAPHOR THAT CONCEDES WHAT THE METHOD CANNOT SEE: most of the model's computation **RUNS OUTSIDE THE J-SPACE**, and so what the graphs capture is **THE VERBALIZABLE SKELETON OF THE COMPUTATION RATHER THAN THE WHOLE OF IT**. The instrument's reach is named as a part of its object, not as a defect of the study
span.quote: most of the model's computation runs outside the J-space, and so what the graphs capture is the verbalizable skeleton of the computation rather than the whole of it.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AND THE PROPERTIES THE ANALOGY DOES NOT ESTABLISH ARE LISTED AS ABSENT: note that there are **OTHER STRUCTURAL PROPERTIES ASSOCIATED WITH GLOBAL WORKSPACE THEORY THAT ARE NOT DEMONSTRATED BY OUR ANALYSES**. A borrowed framework is adopted in part, and the unadopted part is named rather than left for a reader to notice
span.quote: note that there are other structural properties associated with global workspace theory that are not demonstrated by our analyses.

span.label: The lens is acknowledged as an approximate and incomplete proxy for whatever the model's real workspace is.
span.quote: The Jacobian lens is an imperfect tool, which we believe only approximately and incompletely captures the model’s underlying workspace structure.

span.label: It can only name concepts that happen to be single tokens in the vocabulary.
span.quote: This construction means that the set of concepts the lens can name is exactly the set of concepts that have a single-token name in the tokenizer's vocabulary.

span.label: The readout is a flat bag of concepts and cannot show how they are bound or structured together.
span.quote: Even setting the vocabulary issue aside, the J-lens treats the workspace as a flat collection of independently active concept vectors.

span.label: Readouts are not always interpretable, and the rate of uninterpretable ones was not characterised systematically.
span.quote: In our experience this is the typical case at workspace-layer positions, but it is not the universal one: at some positions and layers, the top lens tokens are ones we cannot make sense of.

span.label: The apparent emptiness of the early layers may be a fact about the model or an artefact of the lens; the authors cannot tell which.
span.quote: W e do not know whether this is a fact about the model or an artifact of the lens.

span.label: No mechanism is offered for how a representation comes to enter the workspace.
span.quote: W e have not characterized what causes a representation to enter it.

span.label: The authors decline to claim the J-space is sufficient for alignment monitoring, since automatic or well-practised misaligned behaviour could bypass it.
span.quote: W e do not feel comfortable making the stronger claim that monitoring the J-space is sufficient for alignment monitoring, or that any sophisticated plan the model might execute must be represented there.

span.label: Findings are from large production models only; scaling and training-time emergence are untested.
span.quote: W e have studied the workspace primarily in fully trained production LLMs of considerable size.

span.label: The analogy to global workspace theory is explicitly partial: architectural features such as encapsulated processors and recurrent broadcast are not claimed.
span.quote: Despite these similarities, we do not claim that language models reproduce the full architecture global workspace theory ascribes to the brain

span.label: a positive control on the ablation itself, checking it removes the content the J-space was shown to carry
span.quote: W e first verify, as a positive control, that the ablation removes the kind of content the preceding sections showed the J-space to carry.

span.label: a story-writing task run under the same ablation, scoring general story quality alongside the rate of experiential language
span.quote: A story-writing control confirms the effect is not due to broad degradation of writing capability: ablation only slightly reduces graded story quality, while still reducing the rate of experiential language within those stories ( §A.23 ).

span.label: zeroing equal-sized, layer-matched sets of randomly chosen heads - the sentence states the control and not its outcome, so no outcome is recorded here
span.quote: W e zero the heads' outputs at every token position, and as a control we do the same to equal-sized, layer-matched sets of randomly chosen heads.

span.label: a perturbation of equal magnitude applied to a different concept of the same category
span.quote: As a control, to ensure the effect on avoidance behavior is not simply due to perturbations generically degrading the model’s capabilities, or due to noise leading to regression-to-mean effects, we tried applying a perturbation of equal magnitude, inhibiting the J-lens vector of some other concept of the same category as the primed one.

span.label: global workspace
span.quote: A representation becomes consciously accessible when it is posted to a shared "global workspace" from which many downstream processes can read .

span.label: consciously accessible information
span.quote: Several functional properties are commonly held to distinguish consciously accessible information from unconscious processing.

span.label: single-token name
span.quote: This construction means that the set of concepts the lens can name is exactly the set of concepts that have a single-token name in the tokenizer's vocabulary.

span.label: global workspace - the theory's sense: a shared space a representation is posted to, from which many downstream processes can read
span.quote: A representation becomes consciously accessible when it is posted to a shared "global workspace" from which many downstream processes can read .

span.label: global workspace - a processing hub that integrates and broadcasts, so the information can be used for flexible internal reasoning and report
span.quote: Under the theory, the workspace is a processing hub that integrates and broadcasts information, allowing it to be used for flexible internal reasoning and report .

span.label: nameable concept - bounded by the tokenizer: exactly those concepts holding a single-token name, which is what the lens can report at all
span.quote: This construction means that the set of concepts the lens can name is exactly the set of concepts that have a single-token name in the tokenizer's vocabulary.

span.label: global workspace - what the paper explicitly does NOT claim language models reproduce
span.quote: we do not claim that language models reproduce the full architecture global workspace theory ascribes to the brain

span.label: extends → the logit lens
span.quote: While the logit lens assumes that representations use the same coordinates in all layers, the Jacobian lens corrects for representational changes that take place across layers, allowing it to uncover meaningful information in earlier layers where the logit lens produces uninterpretable readouts.

span.label: builds-on → Hernandez et al., per-relation linear maps from Jacobians
span.quote: The J-lens applies the same first-order approximation to the map from activations to model outputs, rather than to a single relation.

span.label: replicates → Li et al., logit-lens decoding and patching of multi-hop intermediates
span.quote: Closest to our approach, Li et al. use the logit lens to decode the intermediate entity in a multi-hop query from middle layers and patch along the decoded directions to redirect the answer, paralleling the internal-reasoning results of §3.3 .

span.label: builds-on → work on implicit chain-of-thought
span.quote: More closely related to our method is work on “implicit chain-of-thought” , which establishes that training on auxiliary reasoning text can shape computation in that context, even when the auxiliary text is dropped at inference.

span.label: consciously accessible information —operationalised-as→ global workspace
span.quote: A representation becomes consciously accessible when it is posted to a shared "global workspace" from which many downstream processes can read .

span.label: LLMs maintain a privileged set of internal representations available for report, modulation, and flexible reasoning
span.quote: language models maintain a privileged set of internal representations, available for report, modulation, and flexible internal reasoning

span.label: an analogous accessible/unconscious functional distinction has emerged in modern AI models
span.quote: an analogous functional distinction has emerged in modern AI

span.label: a new interpretability technique surfaces the concepts a model is poised to verbalize
span.quote: a new interpretability technique, which surfaces the concepts a model is poised

span.label: verbalizable vs automatic internal representations
span.quote: the concepts a model is poised

span.label: global workspace (LLM analog)
span.quote: a privileged set of internal representations, available for report, modulation, and flexible internal reasoning
